title: K-flatness of the point extension of a flat-term module complex
statement: Let k be any field and let R, B, alpha, L and its sections adjunction be the ordinary point-extension models [def-pod-point-derived-hom-models], with L identified on objects and morphisms with B tensor over the constant R-sheaf of the constant module. Let c be an unbounded R-module complex for which Tot(F tensor_R c) is acyclic for every acyclic R-module complex F, and suppose every c^p is a flat R-module. Then Lc is K-flat in the independent-coefficient sheaf-module sense [def-pc-kflat-complex]. No exactness of L or sections is assumed.

proof.text: Identify ordinary R-modules with sheaves of modules on the one-object site with its trivial topology. The constant-sheaf functor is left adjoint to sections at the final object: a map out of a constant presheaf is determined by that component. Constant presheaves preserve finite limits, and associated sheafification is left exact.

Construct the induced algebraic inverse image and identify its modules and scalar extension along alpha with L using the specified object and morphism equalities. Transport tensor, flatness and acyclicity across the equivalence on the one-object site. Apply ringed-topos pullback of flat-term K-flat complexes to obtain K-flatness of Lc.
